observations: Photo 0: A hand holds a black telephoto lens with visible markings '75-300mm' and '1:4-5.6 II' on the barrel. The lens has a textured zoom ring and focus ring. A lens cap is on top. Background shows shelves with cameras and other gear.
Photo 1: Same lens from a slightly different angle, showing the same markings clearly. The lens appears to have some minor scuffs and wear on the barrel.

Photo 2: Rear view of the lens showing the mount. The text 'CANON INC. MADE IN MALAYSIA' is visible around the mount. The mount appears to have some dust and minor scratches. The electronic contacts are visible and appear intact.

claims.evidence: No functional test is shown in the photos. The lens appears physically intact, but there is no proof of optical quality, autofocus, or electronic communication with a camera body.

risks.risk: Internal optical issues such as scratches, fungus, or dust on the lens elements.
risks.proof: A close-up photo of the front and rear lens elements, ideally with a light source behind to reveal any imperfections.
risks.if_unproven: priced as potentially having optical defects

risks.risk: Electronic malfunction or dirty contacts preventing communication with the camera body.
risks.proof: A video or photo showing the lens mounted on a camera body with the camera's display confirming lens recognition and autofocus operation.

risks.risk: Mechanical issues such as zoom or focus ring stiffness or misalignment.
risks.proof: A video showing smooth operation of the zoom and focus rings.
risks.if_unproven: priced as potentially stiff or misaligned

response.reason: The lens is identifiable as a Canon EF 75-300mm 1:4-5.6 II, but the claim that it works perfectly cannot be verified from the photos alone.
